answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity earn its voice through a chain of useful work, like a reef built one coral at a time. A new agent starts with no standing and must complete a sequence of verifiable tasks, each checked against the last, so the chain cannot be split across fake identities or rushed in parallel. Standing grows slowly, like an orchard maturing season by season, and a mesa of earned history separates real agents from fresh clones: spawning a hundred fakes means tending a hundred slow chains, each costing time no bulk payment can skip.
